name: explorer
description: A Vite-native testing framework. It's fast!

works: Activates in a workspace with a Vitest config or vitest in node_modules and starts Vitest from the project
Test Explorer tree: the Testing view in the sidebar shows folders, test files, suites and tests; a file's tests load when it is expanded
Filter the tree by text, !exclude or @vitest:tag; Enter or Go to Test (Alt+Enter) opens the test in the editor
Update Snapshot in a test's context menu runs Vitest with snapshot updates for that test
Test: Refresh Tests (Ctrl+; Ctrl+R) reloads the Vitest configs, Test: Cancel Test Refresh stops it
Run Tests in the Testing view, Run Test on a row, reruns and Cancel Test Run: passed, failed and skipped tests with durations, the results summary
Test Results panel with output: opens on a run with the run's tree and failure messages, and Vitest's colored output of the run or of the chosen test
Failure messages with an expected/actual diff in the Test Results panel, the stack frames under them (a click opens the file at the line), Go to Error and Copy Error
Editor gutter: a run glyph on each test's line, the test's state after a run, a click runs the test, a right click opens its menu
Inline failure messages: a failed assertion's message after its line in the editor, a click opens it in the Test Results panel
Run at cursor: Test: Run Test at Cursor (Ctrl+; C), Run Tests in Current File (Ctrl+; F), Go to Next/Previous Test Failure (Alt+F8/Shift+Alt+F8)
limits: No debugging: Diode has no debugger
No coverage: coverage is not shown
No continuous run: Vitest's watch mode is not offered
No peek view: failure messages open in the Test Results panel

readme:
# Vitest

The official Vitest extension: discovers the tests of a Vitest project so the editor can show and run them.

This is the unmodified extension published on Open VSX, pinned to a specific version.

In Diode the Testing view shows and runs the tests, and the Test Results panel shows their output. The extension needs Vitest installed in the project (`node_modules`).
